label: Diagram 2.1
caption: Diagram 2.1
description:
Four sections through dwellinghouses, a. to d., each with a pitched roof over an 'Unoccupied space'. Green arrows show the 'Direction of escape'; grey shading is a 'Protected stairway (minimum REI 30)'. See paras 2.1 to 2.6.

a. 'Single storey dwellinghouse (see paragraph 2.1)': 'Escape via entrance hall. Inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors.'

b. 'Dwellinghouse with upper storeys a maximum of 4.5m above ground level (see paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3)': two storeys, with '4.5m max.' marked from the ground. Upper storey: 'Escape via stair and escape windows. Alternatively provide a protected stairway.' Ground storey: escape via entrance hall, inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors.

c. 'Dwellinghouse with one storey more than 4.5m above ground level (see paragraph 2.5)': three storeys beside a protected stairway, with '4.5m' marked from the ground. Top: 'Escape via protected stairway. No inner rooms allowed.' Middle: 'Escape via protected stairway. Inner rooms provided with escape windows.' Ground: escape via entrance hall, inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors.

d. 'Dwellinghouse with two or more storeys more than 4.5m above ground level (see paragraph 2.6)': four storeys beside a protected stairway, with '4.5m' and '7.5m' marked from the ground. Top: 'Escape via protected stairway. Provide alternative escape route or sprinklers. No inner rooms allowed.' Next: protected stairway, no inner rooms. Next: protected stairway, inner rooms provided with escape windows. Ground: escape via entrance hall.
model_description:
This drawing, titled "Diagram 2.1 Means of escape from dwellinghouses", consists of four cross-section diagrams (a, b, c, and d) depicting different dwellinghouse configurations and their escape routes.

Diagram a shows a "Single storey dwellinghouse (see paragraph 2.1)". It features an "Unoccupied space" in the roof and an "Escape via entrance hall" where "Inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors" are shown with green arrows indicating the "Direction of escape".

Diagram b shows a "Dwellinghouse with upper storeys a maximum of 4.5m above ground level (see paragraphs 2.2 and 2.3)". It includes an "Unoccupied space", an "Escape via stair and escape windows" or an alternative "protected stairway", and an "Escape via entrance hall" with "Inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors". A dimension of "4.5m max." is shown.

Diagram c shows a "Dwellinghouse with one storey more than 4.5m above ground level (see paragraph 2.5)". It includes an "Unoccupied space", an "Escape via protected stairway" where "No inner rooms allowed", and an "Escape via entrance hall" with "Inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors". A height dimension of "4.5m" is indicated.

Diagram d shows a "Dwellinghouse with two or more storeys more than 4.5m above ground level (see paragraph 2.6)". It features an "Unoccupied space", an upper level "Escape via protected stairway" where "Provide alternative escape route or sprinklers. No inner rooms allowed", a middle level "Escape via protected stairway. Inner rooms provided with escape windows", and a bottom level "Escape via entrance hall. Inner rooms provided with escape windows or doors". Dimensions of "7.5m" and "4.5m" are provided.
